findings.cross_file_justification: The gate in loader.py is consumed by the diff-touched agy adapter's complete()/health_check()/validate_config() with no project_root argument, so the decision is made from _find_project_root() (the cwd walk) at dispatch time.
findings.description: The new opt-in gate is meant to ensure the argv-prompt exposure is 'only ever exposed by an operator's deliberate choice' and explicitly refuses environment overrides. But the gate is evaluated from the cwd walk at each complete() call, and the adapter's own docstring notes the caller's cwd during a review is the reviewed tree. A `.loa.config.yaml` that lives in (or is added to) the tree being reviewed with `hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in: true` therefore flips the route on. The test `test_the_adapter_reads_the_real_project_config` confirms a chdir into any directory carrying the key enables dispatch. The same ambient-trust problem the docstring rejects for env vars is present for cwd-derived config: a PR/branch under review can opt the reviewer into putting the (redacted) diff on argv, readable via /proc/<pid>/cmdline by other local users, and into spawning `agy --dangerously-skip-permissions` on hosts where it is installed.
findings.failure_mode: Untrusted review content (the tree being reviewed) controls a security-relevant operator decision; the opt-in gate can be bypassed by anyone who can land a config file in the reviewed checkout, defeating the stated intent of FR-1.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve the opt-in from the operator's own config root rather than the per-call cwd walk: pin project_root once at cheval startup (the invoking tool's root, not the reviewed tree) and pass it through to the adapter, or read the key only from the System-defaults layer / an operator-owned location outside the reviewed checkout. At minimum, document that the reviewed tree's .loa.config.yaml is trusted for this key and have the one-time WARN state which file enabled it.

findings.description: The new shared argv builder appends `--effort <effort>` for any truthy string without validating it against the known effort levels. In cheval.py the CLI-level `resolve_effort` validates against _EFFORT_LEVELS, but the adapter calls `build_headless_argv(..., effort=self._resolve_effort(request, model_config))`, and `_resolve_effort` also reads the catalog's `extra.effort`/`extra.reasoning_effort` legacy rungs. A catalog value such as `--dangerously-skip-permissions` or `--permission-mode` would be placed verbatim as a separate argv token after `--effort`, which the CLI's option parser may interpret as a flag rather than a value. This is operator-controlled config, so it is a hardening gap rather than an exploitable path, but the builder is now also used by tools/ceiling-probe-live.py and will be the single chokepoint for future callers.
findings.failure_mode: A malformed or hostile catalog effort value could alter headless CLI flags (e.g. weakening plan mode or tool restrictions) instead of being rejected.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate `effort` inside build_headless_argv against the same allowed set used by cheval.resolve_effort (reuse `_EFFORT_LEVELS` or a shared constant) and raise ConfigError / drop the flag with a WARN when it is not one of the known levels; reject any value starting with '-'.
